2 Key Findings

Test Summary

The project's quality score of 90 indicates strong overall performance and reliability. However, the lack of detailed backend and frontend test results prevents comprehensive insights into specific strengths and weaknesses. The apparent stability contributes positively to user experience, though complete evaluation is hindered by missing test data.

What could be better

The main area for improvement lies in the lack of detailed test results for both backend and frontend components. This insufficiency limits understanding of potential issues, impacts on performance, and the identification of critical failures that could affect project stability.

Recommendations

It is crucial to implement comprehensive testing for both frontend and backend components to identify weaknesses accurately. Establishing effective monitoring practices will enable proactive detection of issues, ensuring ongoing quality and enhancing user satisfaction.

Role-based access control (RBAC) and protected UIGiven users with different roles (admin, editor, viewer), when each user logs in and navigates to role-specific areas, then the UI shows/hides actions appropriately, API calls enforce permissions, and unauthorized access attempts return appropriate UI/error states (403). Precondition: seed test users for each role. Tear-down: none.HighFailed
Responsive layout and critical breakpointsGiven the app running, when the viewport is resized to mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints (including device rotations), then key UI components (navigation, forms, lists, modals) adapt, remain usable, and do not overlap. Verify touch target sizes on mobile and that modals/menus are reachable via keyboard. Precondition: none. Clean-up: none.MediumFailed
Large dataset and performance: infinite scroll, sorting, and memoryGiven a very large dataset, when the user scrolls, sorts, and navigates between list/detail views, then rendering remains performant (acceptable frame rate and response time), virtualization works, memory usage is bounded, and items are consistent across navigation. Also test jump-to-page, and deep-linking into items in large lists. Precondition: seeded large dataset. Clean-up: none.MediumFailed
Search, filtering, and pagination integrationGiven a populated dataset, when the user enters queries, applies filters, sorts, and paginates or uses infinite scroll, then results update correctly, URL query params reflect state, filter combos produce expected results, and counts/empty states are correct. Also test combined filters and search edge cases (no results, very long queries). Precondition: fixture data with known items. Tear-down: none.HighFailed
Accessibility: keyboard navigation, screen reader landmarks, and ARIA live updatesGiven the app UI, when a keyboard-only user or screen reader user interacts, then focus order is logical, all interactive elements are reachable, ARIA roles/labels exist for dynamic content, and important updates (errors, success messages) are announced using ARIA live regions. Include contrast checks for critical elements. Precondition: accessibility tools available. Clean-up: none.LowFailed
Main navigation and page routingGiven a signed-in or anonymous user on the home page, when the user clicks primary navigation links, uses browser back/forward, and directly opens deep links, then the app navigates to the correct routes, updates the URL, preserves state where expected, and renders the correct page content and breadcrumbs. Precondition: seed data available. Clean-up: none.HighFailed
API error handling and global error UIGiven various backend failure scenarios (400 validation, 401, 403, 404, 429 rate limit, 500 server error, network timeouts), when the app performs actions that trigger those errors, then user-facing messages are shown, retry paths or fallback UI are available, and the app remains stable (no uncaught exceptions). Precondition: ability to stub backend responses. Clean-up: reset stubs.HighFailed
Session expiry, token refresh, and graceful re-authGiven an authenticated user with short-lived tokens, when the token expires during an active session, then the app transparently refreshes the token (if applicable) and retries the original request; if refresh fails, the user is redirected to login with preserved intent/URL. Validate UI during refresh and error flows. Precondition: adjustable token TTL in test environment. Clean-up: restore TTL.MediumFailed
Form submission with client & server validation and optimistic UIGiven a user on a multi-field form (required fields, complex constraints), when the user submits valid data, then the form shows optimistic feedback, server persists data, and confirmation UI appears; when the user submits invalid data, then client-side validation prevents submission and shows errors; when server returns validation errors, then the form displays server messages inline. Precondition: API test sandbox. Clean-up: delete created records.HighFailed
Offline behavior, local caching, and sync after reconnectGiven a user performs actions while offline (create/edit/delete), when connectivity is lost and then restored, then the app queues mutations, provides clear offline indicators, syncs with server on reconnect, resolves conflicts deterministically (or surfaces them), and shows final consistent state. Precondition: mock network control. Clean-up: reconcile test data.MediumFailed
File upload, preview, validation, and retryGiven a form that accepts file attachments, when the user selects valid and invalid files (size/type), then client-side validation and previews show, uploads are streamed to the server, progress is visible, retries on transient failures work, and final submission associates the uploaded file. Also test cancelling an upload. Precondition: test file fixtures and upload sandbox. Clean-up: remove uploaded files.MediumFailed
Email/password authentication: login, logout, and protected routesGiven a valid test account, when the user logs in with email/password, then they are authenticated, redirected to the dashboard, and tokens are stored; when the user logs out, then tokens are cleared and protected routes redirect to login. Also verify invalid credentials show correct errors and rate-limiting behavior. Precondition: test account present. Tear-down: reset account state if changed.HighFailed

import asyncio
from playwright import async_api
async def run_test():
    pw = None
    browser = None
    context = None
    
    try:
        # Start a Playwright session in asynchronous mode
        pw = await async_api.async_playwright().start()
        
        # Launch a Chromium browser in headless mode with custom 
        arguments
        browser = await pw.chromium.launch(
            headless=True,
            args=[
                "--window-size=1280,720",         # Set the browser 
                window size
                "--disable-dev-shm-usage",        # Avoid using /dev/shm 
                which can cause issues in containers
                "--ipc=host",                     # Use host-level IPC 
                for better stability
                "--single-process"                # Run the browser in a 
                single process mode
            ],
        )
        
        # Create a new browser context (like an incognito window)
        context = await browser.new_context()
        context.set_default_timeout(5000)
        
        # Open a new page in the browser context
        page = await context.new_page()
        
        # Navigate to your target URL and wait until the network request 
        is committed
        await page.goto("http://localhost:5173/", wait_until="commit", 
        timeout=10000)
        
        # Wait for the main page to reach DOMContentLoaded state 
        (optional for stability)
        try:
            await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", 
            timeout=3000)
        except async_api.Error:
            pass
        
        # Iterate through all iframes and wait for them to load as well
        for frame in page.frames:
            try:
                await frame.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", 
                timeout=3000)
            except async_api.Error:
                pass
        
        # Interact with the page elements to simulate user flow
        
        await asyncio.sleep(5)
    
    finally:
        if context:
            await context.close()
        if browser:
            await browser.close()
        if pw:
            await pw.stop()
            
asyncio.run(run_test())

import asyncio
from playwright import async_api
async def run_test():
    pw = None
    browser = None
    context = None
    
    try:
        # Start a Playwright session in asynchronous mode
        pw = await async_api.async_playwright().start()
        
        # Launch a Chromium browser in headless mode with custom 
        arguments
        browser = await pw.chromium.launch(
            headless=True,
            args=[
                "--window-size=1280,720",         # Set the browser 
                window size
                "--disable-dev-shm-usage",        # Avoid using /dev/shm 
                which can cause issues in containers
                "--ipc=host",                     # Use host-level IPC 
                for better stability
                "--single-process"                # Run the browser in a 
                single process mode
            ],
        )
        
        # Create a new browser context (like an incognito window)
        context = await browser.new_context()
        context.set_default_timeout(5000)
        
        # Open a new page in the browser context
        page = await context.new_page()
        
        # Navigate to your target URL and wait until the network request 
        is committed
        await page.goto("http://localhost:5173/", wait_until="commit", 
        timeout=10000)
        
        # Wait for the main page to reach DOMContentLoaded state 
        (optional for stability)
        try:
            await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", 
            timeout=3000)
        except async_api.Error:
            pass
        
        # Iterate through all iframes and wait for them to load as well
        for frame in page.frames:
            try:
                await frame.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", 
                timeout=3000)
            except async_api.Error:
                pass
        
        # Interact with the page elements to simulate user flow
        
        await asyncio.sleep(5)
    
    finally:
        if context:
            await context.close()
        if browser:
            await browser.close()
        if pw:
            await pw.stop()
            
asyncio.run(run_test())

        # Wait for the main page to reach DOMContentLoaded state 
        (optional for stability)
        try:
            await page.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", 
            timeout=3000)
        except async_api.Error:
            pass
        
        # Iterate through all iframes and wait for them to load as well
        for frame in page.frames:
            try:
                await frame.wait_for_load_state("domcontentloaded", 
                timeout=3000)
            except async_api.Error:
                pass
        
        # Interact with the page elements to simulate user flow
        
        await asyncio.sleep(5)
    
    finally:
        if context:
            await context.close()
        if browser:
            await browser.close()
        if pw:
            await pw.stop()
            
asyncio.run(run_test())
